why: the reviewer found that MAX_TURNS was 10 while the nominal call count of the new shape is 13; a model that issues single reads would have hit MaxTurnsExceeded and been truncated in one arm only, which is the asymmetry this design exists to avoid. The protocol now requires each round's three reads in one turn, MAX_TURNS admits the single-read path, and the cap is re-derived from the new worst case

registry_changes.new_text:
return [
        "Call three read-only tools in each of "
        f"{READ_ROUNDS} rounds, in this order, and never read the same registered view twice: "
        + "; ".join(rounds)
        + f". That is {READ_CALLS} read calls over {len(views)} distinct registered views.",
        "Issue the three calls of a round together in one turn, as a single batch of three "
        "calls, and wait for their results before starting the next round. Do not split a round "

runner_changes.label: max_turns_admits_the_legal_single_read_path
runner_changes.new_text:
#: twelve reads, an answer and a retry must all fit: the protocol asks for four
#: batches, but a model that issues single reads still needs twelve turns, and
#: truncating one arm silently is exactly the asymmetry this design must avoid.
MAX_TURNS = registry.READ_CALLS + 2

runner_changes.new_text:
samples = len(registry.task_ids()) * PILOT_REPEATS * len(PILOT_METHODS)
    #: the four-round shape issues four read batches and one answer turn per sample when the
    #: protocol is followed, and twelve reads, an answer and a retry when it is not
    measured_low, measured_high = 2.67, 3.0
    expected_per_sample = registry.READ_ROUNDS + 1
    expected = samples * expected_per_sample
    worst_per_sample = MAX_TURNS + live.RETRY_BUDGET_PER_SAMPLE
    worst_calls = samples * worst_per_sample
